page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-240GB-1xB200 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8570 processor. It features 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 240 GB of system memory, providing 10 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU containing 192 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in LLM inference tasks, with prompt processing reaching 9953.26 tokens per second and text generation achieving 525.92 tokens per second on a small 135M model. Memory bandwidth is strong, measuring 251.17 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 115.78 GB/sec for write operations. CPU capabilities are supported by advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for tile and int8 operations, contributing to a strong Passmark CPU score of 52754.5 and an extended instructions score of 67506.68.

The server offers high resource density by pairing a massive 192 GB GPU frame buffer with 240 GB of system memory, making it highly efficient for memory-intensive accelerator workloads. Tradeoffs include the shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.

This configuration is designed for large language model inference, deep learning training, and complex data science workloads that require substantial GPU memory. It is also suitable for cryptographic processing, high-throughput database operations, and memory-bound parallel computing tasks.
